title: Garden Salad with Chicken or Turkey, Cheese, Lettuce and Vegetables, No Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: The garden salad combines cooked or roasted chicken and/or turkey breast, mild cheese, lettuce or mixed greens, tomatoes and/or carrots, and other fresh vegetables. It is served without dressing, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are lean sources of high‑quality protein that are easily digested.
Cheese adds calcium and a creamy texture to the salad.
Leafy greens provide vitamins A, C, K and folate.
Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that is even more bioavailable when cooked, but still beneficial fresh.
The lack of dressing makes the dish low‑calorie and suitable for diet plans.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey supply essential amino acids needed for muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium and phosphorus, important for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Tomatoes and carrots are high in beta‑carotene and lycopene, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: Vitamin C from tomatoes and greens enhances the body’s immune response.

items.title: Low in unhealthy fats
items.content: Without dressing and using lean meat, the salad is low in saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improperly cooked or stored chicken/turkey can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Some cheeses are salty, which should be considered by those limiting sodium intake.

items.title: Nutrient interactions
items.content: Large amounts of cheese can inhibit iron absorption from leafy greens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled. It can be enjoyed as a standalone meal or as a side dish. If desired, add a light drizzle of lemon juice or balsamic vinegar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, store protein, cheese, and vegetables separately to prevent the leaves from becoming soggy.
